A VPN (virtual private network) is a connection that sends your internet traffic through a private, scrambled tunnel to a computer run by the VPN company, before it reaches the website or app you're using.

Because the traffic is scrambled, anyone on the same Wi-Fi, like at a café or airport, can't read what you send. Websites also see the VPN company's address instead of yours, which hides your real location and makes tracking you harder.

A VPN doesn't make you anonymous or fully safe. The VPN company can see your traffic, so pick one you trust, and avoid free ones that earn money by selling your data. It also won't protect you from fake websites or bad downloads.

results.lastReply:
VPN (virtual private network) ek private raasta hai jo aapka internet traffic scramble karke VPN company ke computer se guzaarta hai, aur phir website ya app tak pahunchata hai.

Traffic scramble hone ki wajah se café ya airport ke Wi-Fi par koi aapka data padh nahi sakta. Websites ko aapke address ki jagah VPN company ka address dikhta hai, isse aapki asli location chhupti hai aur tracking mushkil hoti hai.

VPN aapko poori tarah anonymous ya safe nahi banata. VPN company aapka traffic dekh sakti hai, isliye bharosemand company chuniye aur free VPN se bachiye, kyunki woh aksar aapka data bechkar kamaate hain. Yeh nakli websites ya galat downloads se bhi nahi bachata.
